text.tspan: Snow, Lamp, Bridge: sound map, top-down
Generated from src/audio/cues.js (149 cues), SHOTS and spatial.js. Sound 1 storyboard, for your markup. North is up.
the car's sounds (39): stop, doors, getting out, ticks
background, unplaced: city -7.0, wind -1.0 dB, sum 0.0 dB
background, unplaced: city -7.0, water -3.5, wind +0.5 dB, sum +2.5 dB
wind from 70 deg, and the water: unplaced, bridge only
Steps: one label per walker on this map; each step's contact time is on the
Wedge: field of view at the shot's start, dashed at its end. The line through
the camera is its left and right axis, the head at its right. Shaded half-disc:
behind the camera, -2.5 dB and darker (behindGain 0.75, air x 0.45). Rings,
over the half in front: where each law has fallen by -6, -12, -18 and -24 dB,
for the laws its shot's cues use; this map leaves out rings past 25 m (the
Predicted level, in dB on the level plan's scale (SOUND-PLAN 1.3; on it the
background beds sum to 0.0 dB on the street and +2.5 dB on the bridge) =
the cue's designed level + 20 log10(gain) + its modifiers. Gain and pan from
spatial.placeAt at the cue's place under LAWS[cue.law], heard from the
camera playing at that moment. Modifiers (car rises out of the quiet, car
swells as it comes in, wind eases, night opens) change the families they
name from their onset by their track: the rise from its level up to 0, the others
from 0 to their level, held after their end. The background playing is drawn at
its own level; read a cue against it. Unplaced beds: no pan.
